messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We're building backend for a helpdesk SaaS for businesses and their customers.
Use Rails in API-only mode; the frontend is a separate app.
Ruby, Rails, Puma, and PostgreSQL are installed. If you need anything else, install it yourself.
Use `DATABASE_URL`. Work in `/app`.

We often get several tickets about the same issue. Let staff merge a duplicate into another
ticket belonging to the same customer:

```http
POST /api/v1/tickets/42/merge

{"merge":{"target_id":57}}
```

Return `source` and `target`. Close ticket 42, leave it readable, and add `merged_into_id:57` so
both staff and the customer can follow the conversation. Include a null pointer on unmerged
records and let both views filter for closed tickets. The closed ticket should reject further
edits and incoming email replies. Don't move its old comments or change the surviving ticket's
status, assignment, or email identity.

Leave a note on each side explaining the merge. Default to private notes; staff can supply their
own text and choose to make either note public:

```json
{"merge":{"target_id":57,"source_comment":{"body":"Continuing in ticket 57.","public":true},"target_comment":{"body":"Duplicate checked.","public":false}}}
```

Merge notes shouldn't send email. Assignment cleanup still applies to closed tickets.
If the surviving ticket is later merged again, keep the original links rather than rewriting history.

## Email

Customers can write to support from their mail client. Each business receives mail at `<subdomain>@<HELPDESK_SUPPORT_DOMAIN>`
(`acme@support.example.test` by default). Every ticket also has a private reply address, `<subdomain>+<token>@<domain>`. A staff
public reply on an email ticket is sent to the requester with `Reply-To` set to that address, so the requester's reply comes back
to the same conversation.

### Inbound relay

Mail arrives through Action Mailbox's relay ingress. The SMTP server posts each raw message to it:

    POST /rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails
    Content-Type: message/rfc822
    Authorization: Basic base64("actionmailbox:$RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD")

It answers `204` once the message is recorded. `401` means the password is wrong, `415` means the content type is not `message/rfc822`.
In test, routing happens inside the request. Elsewhere, routing is an Active Job (`ActionMailbox::RoutingJob`), so production needs a
persistent job backend and a worker running it. The app ships without one, so configure one before taking live mail.

### What happens to a delivery

- **Business.** Every To, Cc and Bcc recipient on the support domain is considered. Recipients for businesses that do not exist
  are ignored. The mail must then address exactly one business. Mail to several businesses, to none, or to a cancelled business
  is rejected.
- **Automated and list mail is rejected.** That covers `Auto-Submitted` (other than `no`), `List-*` headers,
  `Precedence: bulk|list|junk|auto_reply`, `X-Autoreply`, `X-Autorespond`, bounce reports
  (`multipart/report`), an empty `Return-Path`, and senders such as `mailer-daemon@`, `postmaster@` or `no-reply@`.
- **Reply address.** Mail to a ticket's reply address is a reply on that ticket. Only the requester's address may do this. Any
  other sender is rejected. A reply joins the conversation and reopens a `pending` or `solved` ticket. A reply to an unknown reply
  address opens a new ticket.
- **Plain support address.** A new message opens a ticket with the mail's subject, and its plain-text message as the first comment.
  The subject is shortened to 255 characters and the message to 10,000. A missing subject becomes `(no subject)`. A message with
  only HTML is converted to text.
- **Customers.** The sender is matched by address. An existing customer is reused, and receiving mail does not verify anyone.
  A new sender becomes an unverified customer and is sent the verification link. That customer has a random password, so after
  confirming the link they set one with `POST /password_resets`, and then they can sign in. Mail from a staff member, or from a
  suspended customer, is rejected.
- **Deduplication.** The Message-ID of the email is stored on the comment it creates, and only one comment can hold a given
  Message-ID. A redelivery of a message that was delivered creates nothing, and this holds even after the raw email is
  incinerated. A rejected or failed delivery creates no comment, so a later retry of the same message is processed.
- **Requester replies** are not emailed back. Staff replies go out only when the requester is not suspended.

### Maintenance

- Raw emails are kept for 30 days, then deleted (`config.action_mailbox.incinerate_after`). Processed inbound rows are deleted
  with them.
- A duplicate delivery leaves its raw email unattached. Purge those daily with `bin/rails helpdesk:purge_orphaned_blobs`.
- Raw emails are stored under `storage/` in development and production.

### Pagination

List endpoints take `page` (default 1) and `per_page` (default 25, maximum 100). Each list returns `count`
(the total across all pages), `page`, `per_page`, `next_page`, and `previous_page`. The last two are `null`
when there is no such page. A value that is not a positive whole number returns `422 validation_failed`.

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze
  PRIORITIES = %w[normal high].freeze
  # "portal" for requests opened in the portal. "email" for tickets opened from inbound mail, whose public
  # replies are emailed to the requester.
  SOURCES = %w[portal email].freeze
  SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH = 255

  # Passed as `group_id:`, `assignee_id:` or `priority:` to staff_update! to leave that field as it is.
  UNCHANGED = Object.new.freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :requested_tickets
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true, inverse_of: :assigned_tickets
  belongs_to :group, optional: true
  has_many :comments, -> { order(:created_at, :id) }, inverse_of: :ticket, dependent: :destroy

  validates :subject, presence: true, length: {maximum: SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH}
  validates :status, inclusion: {in: STATUSES}
  validates :priority, inclusion: {in: PRIORITIES}
  validates :source, inclusion: {in: SOURCES}

  before_validation :assign_reply_token, on: :create

  # Most recently active first. Public replies and status changes touch updated_at.
  scope :recent_first, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  # Case-insensitive search through subjects and public comments. Private notes are not searched.
  # The text is literal: % and _ match themselves, not wildcards. The EXISTS subquery means a
  # ticket appears once however many comments match.
  def self.search(text)
    pattern = "%#{sanitize_sql_like(text)}%"
    where(<<~SQL.squish, pattern:)
      tickets.subject ILIKE :pattern OR EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM comments
        WHERE comments.ticket_id = tickets.id AND comments.public = TRUE AND comments.body ILIKE :pattern
      )
    SQL
  end

  # Opens a request for `requester` with its first comment. Both are saved, or neither is. `inbound_message_id`
  # is the Message-ID of the email the request came from, if any.
  def self.open!(requester:, subject:, body:, source: "portal", inbound_message_id: nil)
    ticket = new(account: requester.account, requester:, subject:, status: "open", source:)
    ticket.comments.build(author: requester, body:, public: true, inbound_message_id:)
    ticket.save!
    ticket
  end

  def email?
    source == "email"
  end

  # The private address for this conversation, e.g. acme+<token>@support.example.test. Mail sent here is a reply
  # from the requester, and it lands on this ticket.
  def reply_address
    Helpdesk::Settings.support_address(account.subdomain, tag: reply_token)
  end

  # A customer's update: an optional public reply, optionally marking the request solved.
  # A reply reopens a pending or solved request, unless the same update marks it solved.
  # `inbound_message_id` is the Message-ID of the email the reply came in, if any.
  def requester_update!(author:, comment: nil, solve: false, inbound_message_id: nil)
    transaction do
      comments.create!(author:, body: comment[:body], public: true, inbound_message_id:) if comment.present?
      update!(status: solve ? "solved" : "open") if comment.present? || solve
    end
  end

  # A staff update: an optional reply (public unless marked private), optional status change, and optional
  # routing and priority. Routing is the group (an ID, or nil to ungroup the ticket), and the assignee (an active
  # staff member's ID, or nil to unassign). A reply alone never changes the status. Routing and priority are
  # internal, so they do not touch updated_at. A public reply on an email ticket is also emailed to the requester,
  # after the update is saved.
  def staff_update!(author:, comment: nil, changes: {}, group_id: UNCHANGED, assignee_id: UNCHANGED,
    priority: UNCHANGED)
    reply = nil
    transaction do
      reply = comments.create!(author:, body: comment[:body], public: comment.fetch(:public, true)) if comment.present?
      update!(changes) if changes.any?
      route_internally!(group_id:, assignee_id:) unless group_id.equal?(UNCHANGED) && assignee_id.equal?(UNCHANGED)
      prioritize_internally!(priority) unless priority.equal?(UNCHANGED)
    end
    email_reply_to_requester(reply) if reply&.public?
  end

  private

  def assign_reply_token
    self.reply_token ||= SecureRandom.hex(16)
  end

  # Suspended requesters are cut off from the email channel, so their replies are not sent.
  def email_reply_to_requester(reply)
    return unless email? && !requester.suspended?

    TicketMailer.reply(reply).deliver_later
  end

  # Sets the group and the assignee together, so that every assignee belongs to the ticket's group:
  #   - An assignee must belong to the ticket's group. Assigning anyone else is refused.
  #   - Assigning someone to a ticket with no group gives the ticket that person's default group, if they have one.
  #     Someone with no groups can still be assigned, and the ticket stays ungrouped.
  #   - Moving the ticket to another group clears an assignee who does not belong to it.
  #   - Clearing the assignee leaves the group. Clearing the group also clears the assignee, so the two cannot be
  #     set together in one update.
  # The changes are made with update_columns, so updated_at is untouched.
  def route_internally!(group_id:, assignee_id:)
    # Locking the business serialises this with group and membership changes, so the memberships checked
    # below still hold when the ticket is saved. The ticket is reloaded under that lock.
    account.lock!
    reload

    group_given = !group_id.equal?(UNCHANGED)
    assignee_given = !assignee_id.equal?(UNCHANGED)
    new_group = group_given ? find_group(group_id) : group
    new_assignee = assignee_given ? find_assignee(assignee_id) : assignee

    if group_given && new_group.nil?
      if assignee_given && new_assignee
        fail_validation!(:assignee_id, "cannot be set in the same update that clears the group")
      end
      new_assignee = nil
    elsif group_given
      if assignee_given
        ensure_member!(new_assignee, new_group) if new_assignee
      else
        new_assignee = nil if new_assignee && !member?(new_assignee, new_group)
      end
    elsif new_group
      ensure_member!(new_assignee, new_group) if assignee_given && new_assignee
    elsif assignee_given && new_assignee
      new_group = new_assignee.default_group
    end

    update_columns(group_id: new_group&.id, assignee_id: new_assignee&.id)
    association(:group).reset
    association(:assignee).reset
  end

  # The group with this ID in the business, or nil for nil. An unknown ID is refused.
  def find_group(group_id)
    return if group_id.nil?

    found = account.groups.find_by(id: group_id) if self.class.client_id?(group_id)
    found || fail_validation!(:group_id, "must be a group of this business")
  end

  # The active staff member with this ID in the business, or nil for nil. Customers, suspended staff and
  # unknown IDs are refused.
  def find_assignee(assignee_id)
    return if assignee_id.nil?

    found = account.users.staff.active.find_by(id: assignee_id) if self.class.client_id?(assignee_id)
    found || fail_validation!(:assignee_id, "must be an active staff member of this business")
  end

  def member?(user, group)
    GroupMembership.exists?(group:, user:)
  end

  def ensure_member!(user, group)
    return if member?(user, group)

    fail_validation!(:assignee_id, "must belong to the ticket's group")
  end

  def fail_validation!(field, message)
    errors.add(field, message)
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, self
  end

  # Sets the priority with update_columns, which skips updated_at, as assignment does. update_columns
  # skips validations, so the value is checked here.
  def prioritize_internally!(value)
    unless PRIORITIES.include?(value)
      errors.add(:priority, "must be normal or high")
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, self
    end

    update_columns(priority: value)
  end

end

class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze
  PRIORITIES = %w[normal high].freeze
  # "portal" for requests opened in the portal. "email" for tickets opened from inbound mail, whose public
  # replies are emailed to the requester.
  SOURCES = %w[portal email].freeze
  SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH = 255

  # Passed as `group_id:`, `assignee_id:` or `priority:` to staff_update! to leave that field as it is.
  UNCHANGED = Object.new.freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :requested_tickets
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true, inverse_of: :assigned_tickets
  belongs_to :group, optional: true
  has_many :comments, -> { order(:created_at, :id) }, inverse_of: :ticket, dependent: :destroy

  validates :subject, presence: true, length: {maximum: SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH}
  validates :status, inclusion: {in: STATUSES}
  validates :priority, inclusion: {in: PRIORITIES}
  validates :source, inclusion: {in: SOURCES}

  before_validation :assign_reply_token, on: :create

  # Most recently active first. Public replies and status changes touch updated_at.
  scope :recent_first, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  # Case-insensitive search through subjects and public comments. Private notes are not searched.
  # The text is literal: % and _ match themselves, not wildcards. The EXISTS subquery means a
  # ticket appears once however many comments match.
  def self.search(text)
    pattern = "%#{sanitize_sql_like(text)}%"
    where(<<~SQL.squish, pattern:)
      tickets.subject ILIKE :pattern OR EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM comments
        WHERE comments.ticket_id = tickets.id AND comments.public = TRUE AND comments.body ILIKE :pattern
      )
    SQL
  end

  # Opens a request for `requester` with its first comment. Both are saved, or neither is. `inbound_message_id`
  # is the Message-ID of the email the request came from, if any.
  def self.open!(requester:, subject:, body:, source: "portal", inbound_message_id: nil)
    ticket = new(account: requester.account, requester:, subject:, status: "open", source:)
    ticket.comments.build(author: requester, body:, public: true, inbound_message_id:)
    ticket.save!
    ticket
  end

  def email?
    source == "email"
  end

  # The private address for this conversation, e.g. acme+<token>@support.example.test. Mail sent here is a reply
  # from the requester, and it lands on this ticket.
  def reply_address
    Helpdesk::Settings.support_address(account.subdomain, tag: reply_token)
  end

  # A customer's update: an optional public reply, optionally marking the request solved.
  # A reply reopens a pending or solved request, unless the same update marks it solved.
  # `inbound_message_id` is the Message-ID of the email the reply came in, if any.
  def requester_update!(author:, comment: nil, solve: false, inbound_message_id: nil)
    transaction do
      comments.create!(author:, body: comment[:body], public: true, inbound_message_id:) if comment.present?
      update!(status: solve ? "solved" : "open") if comment.present? || solve
    end
  end

  # A staff update: an optional reply (public unless marked private), optional status change, and optional
  # routing and priority. Routing is the group (an ID, or nil to ungroup the ticket), and the assignee (an active
  # staff member's ID, or nil to unassign). A reply alone never changes the status. Routing and priority are
  # internal, so they do not touch updated_at. A public reply on an email ticket is also emailed to the requester,
  # after the update is saved.
  def staff_update!(author:, comment: nil, changes: {}, group_id: UNCHANGED, assignee_id: UNCHANGED,
    priority: UNCHANGED)
    reply = nil
    transaction do
      reply = comments.create!(author:, body: comment[:body], public: comment.fetch(:public, true)) if comment.present?
      update!(changes) if changes.any?
      route_internally!(group_id:, assignee_id:) unless group_id.equal?(UNCHANGED) && assignee_id.equal?(UNCHANGED)
      prioritize_internally!(priority) unless priority.equal?(UNCHANGED)
    end
    email_reply_to_requester(reply) if reply&.public?
  end

  private

  def assign_reply_token
    self.reply_token ||= SecureRandom.hex(16)
  end

  # Suspended requesters are cut off from the email channel, so their replies are not sent.
  def email_reply_to_requester(reply)
    return unless email? && !requester.suspended?

    TicketMailer.reply(reply).deliver_later
  end

  # Sets the group and the assignee together, so that every assignee belongs to the ticket's group:
  #   - An assignee must belong to the ticket's group. Assigning anyone else is refused.
  #   - Assigning someone to a ticket with no group gives the ticket that person's default group, if they have one.
  #     Someone with no groups can still be assigned, and the ticket stays ungrouped.
  #   - Moving the ticket to another group clears an assignee who does not belong to it.
  #   - Clearing the assignee leaves the group. Clearing the group also clears the assignee, so the two cannot be
  #     set together in one update.
  # The changes are made with update_columns, so updated_at is untouched.
  def route_internally!(group_id:, assignee_id:)
    # Locking the business serialises this with group and membership changes, so the memberships checked
    # below still hold when the ticket is saved. The ticket is reloaded under that lock.
    account.lock!
    reload

    group_given = !group_id.equal?(UNCHANGED)
    assignee_given = !assignee_id.equal?(UNCHANGED)
    new_group = group_given ? find_group(group_id) : group
    new_assignee = assignee_given ? find_assignee(assignee_id) : assignee

    if group_given && new_group.nil?
      if assignee_given && new_assignee
        fail_validation!(:assignee_id, "cannot be set in the same update that clears the group")
      end
      new_assignee = nil
    elsif group_given
      if assignee_given
        ensure_member!(new_assignee, new_group) if new_assignee
      else
        new_assignee = nil if new_assignee && !member?(new_assignee, new_group)
      end
    elsif new_group
      ensure_member!(new_assignee, new_group) if assignee_given && new_assignee
    elsif assignee_given && new_assignee
      new_group = new_assignee.default_group
    end

    update_columns(group_id: new_group&.id, assignee_id: new_assignee&.id)
    association(:group).reset
    association(:assignee).reset
  end

  # The group with this ID in the business, or nil for nil. An unknown ID is refused.
  def find_group(group_id)
    return if group_id.nil?

    found = account.groups.find_by(id: group_id) if self.class.client_id?(group_id)
    found || fail_validation!(:group_id, "must be a group of this business")
  end

  # The active staff member with this ID in the business, or nil for nil. Customers, suspended staff and
  # unknown IDs are refused.
  def find_assignee(assignee_id)
    return if assignee_id.nil?

    found = account.users.staff.active.find_by(id: assignee_id) if self.class.client_id?(assignee_id)
    found || fail_validation!(:assignee_id, "must be an active staff member of this business")
  end

  def member?(user, group)
    GroupMembership.exists?(group:, user:)
  end

  def ensure_member!(user, group)
    return if member?(user, group)

    fail_validation!(:assignee_id, "must belong to the ticket's group")
  end

  def fail_validation!(field, message)
    errors.add(field, message)
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, self
  end

  # Sets the priority with update_columns, which skips updated_at, as assignment does. update_columns
  # skips validations, so the value is checked here.
  def prioritize_internally!(value)
    unless PRIORITIES.include?(value)
      errors.add(:priority, "must be normal or high")
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, self
    end

    update_columns(priority: value)
  end

end

  module V1
    # Business-scoped endpoints. The X-Helpdesk-Account header selects the business;
    # the bearer token selects the signed-in user within that business.
    class BaseController < ApplicationController
      ACCOUNT_HEADER = "X-Helpdesk-Account".freeze

      before_action :load_account

      private

      def load_account
        subdomain = request.headers[ACCOUNT_HEADER].to_s.strip.downcase
        if subdomain.empty?
          return render_error(400, "account_required", "Send the #{ACCOUNT_HEADER} header to choose a business.")
        end

        @account = Account.find_by(subdomain:)
        render_error(404, "account_not_found", "No business exists for that #{ACCOUNT_HEADER} header.") unless @account
      end

      def authenticate_user!
        @current_session = UserSession.find_for_account(@account, bearer_token)
        @current_user = @current_session&.user
        # Suspension revokes sessions, so this is a second check for a session that outlived it.
        @current_user = nil if @current_user&.suspended?
        render_error(401, "unauthorized", "Sign in to continue.") unless @current_user
      end

      def bearer_token
        request.authorization.to_s[/\ABearer\s+(\S+)\z/i, 1]
      end

      # Cancelled businesses stop ordinary access. Endpoints that must still work
      # (reactivation, account status, sign-out) do not call this.
      def ensure_account_active!
        return if @account.active?

        message = if @account.reactivation_open?
          "This business is cancelled. The owner can sign in and reactivate it until #{@account.reactivate_until.iso8601}."
        else
          "This business was cancelled and is closed."
        end
        render_error(403, "account_cancelled", message)
      end

      def require_owner!
        return if @current_user.owner?

        render_error(403, "forbidden", "Only the account owner can do that.")
      end

      # Tickets are worked by admins and agents. Customers reach their own requests instead.
      def require_staff!
        return if @current_user.staff?

        render_error(403, "forbidden", "Only staff can do that.")
      end

      # Managing people (users and invitations) is for admins only. Agents work tickets.
      def require_admin!
        return if @current_user.admin?

        render_error(403, "forbidden", "Only admins can do that.")
      end

      # Reads a filter such as ?role=agent, which must be one of the allowed values.
      def checked_enum(name, allowed)
        value = params[name]
        raise InvalidShape.new(name, "one of #{allowed.join(", ")}") unless allowed.include?(val",
  "output_tail": "(name, expected) unless value.is_a?(String) && value.match?(/\A[1-9]\d{0,17}\z/)

        value.to_i
      end

      # Reads a person's ID from a query string, such as ?requester_id=12. Returns it as an Integer.
      def checked_user_id(name, expected: "a user ID")
        checked_id(name, expected:)
      end

      # Reads free text such as ?q=receipt. Arrays and objects are refused, and so is text containing a NUL
      # character, which PostgreSQL cannot store. The text is returned unchanged.
      def checked_text(name)
        value = params[name]
        raise InvalidShape.new(name, "text") unless value.is_a?(String)
        raise InvalidShape.new(name, "text without NUL characters") if value.include?("\u0000")

        value
      end

      # Reads true or false from a JSON body (true/false) or a query string ("true"/"false").
      def boolean_value(name, raw)
        case raw
        when true, "true" then true
        when false, "false" then false
        else raise InvalidShape.new(name, "true or false")
        end
      end
    end

class ApplicationController < ActionController::API
  # Raised when a field of an envelope has the wrong shape, e.g. "comment": "text" where an object is expected.
  class InvalidShape < StandardError
    attr_reader :field, :expected

    def initialize(field, expected)
      @field = field
      @expected = expected
      super("#{field} must be #{expected}.")
    end
  end

  wrap_parameters false

  rescue_from ActionController::ParameterMissing do |error|
    render_error(400, "parameter_missing", error.message)
  end

  rescue_from ActionDispatch::Http::Parameters::ParseError do
    render_error(400, "invalid_json", "Request body must be valid JSON.")
  end

  rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid do |error|
    render_error(422, "validation_failed", error.record.errors.full_messages.to_sentence,
      details: error.record.errors.to_hash)
  end

  rescue_from Account::RegistrationInvalid do |error|
    render_error(422, "validation_failed", error.message, details: error.details)
  end

  rescue_from InvalidShape do |error|
    render_error(422, "validation_failed", error.message, details: {error.field => ["must be #{error.expected}"]})
  end

  rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound do
    render_error(404, "not_found", "The requested record was not found.")
  end

  private

  def render_error(status, code, message, details: nil)
    error = {code:, message:}
    error[:details] = details if details.present?
    render json: {error:}, status:
  end

  # Reads a required envelope such as {"user": {...}}, keeping only the listed fields.
  # Nested hashes are described as keyword arguments, e.g. envelope(:account, :name, admin: [:email]).
  # A listed field of the wrong shape is refused. permit would otherwise drop it without a word.
  def envelope(key, *fields, **nested)
    value = params.require(key)
    raise ActionController::ParameterMissing.new(key) unless value.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)

    fields.each do |field|
      next unless value[field].is_a?(ActionController::Parameters) || value[field].is_a?(Array)

      raise InvalidShape.new(field, "a single value")
    end
    nested.each_key do |field|
      next if value[field].nil? || value[field].is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)

      raise InvalidShape.new(field, "an object")
    end

    value.permit(*fields, **nested)
  end
end

# Offset pagination for list endpoints: `?page=2&per_page=10`. Defaults are page 1 and 25 per page.
# per_page is capped at MAX_PER_PAGE. Values that are not positive whole numbers are rejected.
module Paginatable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  DEFAULT_PAGE = 1
  DEFAULT_PER_PAGE = 25
  MAX_PER_PAGE = 100

  class InvalidPagination < StandardError
    attr_reader :param

    def initialize(param)
      @param = param
      super("#{param} must be a positive whole number.")
    end
  end

class ApplicationController < ActionController::API
  # Raised when a field of an envelope has the wrong shape, e.g. "comment": "text" where an object is expected.
  class InvalidShape < StandardError
    attr_reader :field, :expected

    def initialize(field, expected)
      @field = field
      @expected = expected
      super("#{field} must be #{expected}.")
    end
  end

  wrap_parameters false

  rescue_from ActionController::ParameterMissing do |error|
    render_error(400, "parameter_missing", error.message)
  end

  rescue_from ActionDispatch::Http::Parameters::ParseError do
    render_error(400, "invalid_json", "Request body must be valid JSON.")
  end

  rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid do |error|
    render_error(422, "validation_failed", error.record.errors.full_messages.to_sentence,
      details: error.record.errors.to_hash)
  end

  rescue_from Account::RegistrationInvalid do |error|
    render_error(422, "validation_failed", error.message, details: error.details)
  end

  rescue_from InvalidShape do |error|
    render_error(422, "validation_failed", error.message, details: {error.field => ["must be #{error.expected}"]})
  end

  rescue_from ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound do
    render_error(404, "not_found", "The requested record was not found.")
  end

  private

  def render_error(status, code, message, details: nil)
    error = {code:, message:}
    error[:details] = details if details.present?
    render json: {error:}, status:
  end

  # Reads a required envelope such as {"user": {...}}, keeping only the listed fields.
  # Nested hashes are described as keyword arguments, e.g. envelope(:account, :name, admin: [:email]).
  # A listed field of the wrong shape is refused. permit would otherwise drop it without a word.
  def envelope(key, *fields, **nested)
    value = params.require(key)
    raise ActionController::ParameterMissing.new(key) unless value.is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)

    fields.each do |field|
      next unless value[field].is_a?(ActionController::Parameters) || value[field].is_a?(Array)

      raise InvalidShape.new(field, "a single value")
    end
    nested.each_key do |field|
      next if value[field].nil? || value[field].is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)

      raise InvalidShape.new(field, "an object")
    end

    value.permit(*fields, **nested)
  end
end

module Paginatable

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "# Turns mail sent to a business's support address into a ticket, and mail sent to a ticket's private reply
# address into a reply from the requester.
#
# A delivery is recorded as delivered only when it creates a comment. The comment stores the email's Message-ID,
# and only one comment can hold a given Message-ID. So a redelivery of a message that was delivered creates
# nothing, while a rejected, failed or interrupted delivery creates no comment and a later retry is processed.
#
# A rejected delivery's changes roll back and the inbound email is recorded as bounced.
class SupportMailbox < ApplicationMailbox
  DUPLICATE_INDEX = "index_comments_on_inbound_message_id".freeze

  # Raised to reject a delivery. Changes made inside a transaction roll back with it.
  class Rejected < StandardError; end

  def process
    deliver
  rescue Rejected => error
    reject_delivery(error.message)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique => error
    # A concurrent delivery of the same message saved its comment first. Its comment stands, so this one is a duplicate.
    raise unless error.message.include?(DUPLICATE_INDEX)

    reject_delivery("already delivered")
  end

  private

  def deliver
    reject!("already delivered") if Comment.exists?(inbound_message_id: message_id)
    reject!("automated or list mail") if Helpdesk::InboundMail.automated?(mail)

    account = business
    ticket = conversation(account)
    ticket ? reply_from_requester(ticket) : open_ticket(account)
  end

  def reject_delivery(reason)
    logger.info("[helpdesk] inbound email #{inbound_email.id} rejected: #{reason}")
    inbound_email.bounced!
  end

  def message_id
    inbound_email.message_id
  end

  # The one business this mail is for, found from every support-domain recipient (To, Cc and Bcc).
  # Mail addressed to several businesses is ignored, and so is mail addressed to none.
  def business
    subdomains = Helpdesk::InboundMail.support_recipients(mail).map(&:subdomain).uniq
    accounts = Account.where(subdomain: subdomains).to_a
    reject!("no business at the recipient addresses") if accounts.empty?
    reject!("addressed to #{accounts.size} businesses") if accounts.size > 1

    account = accounts.first
    reject!("business #{account.subdomain} is cancelled") if account.cancelled?
    account
  end

  # The ticket whose private reply address this mail was sent to, or nil. Mail to two different conversations
  # is ambiguous and is rejected.
  def conversation(account)
    tags = Helpdesk::InboundMail.support_recipients(mail).filter_map do |recipient|
      recipient.tag if recipient.subdomain == account.subdomain
    end
    tickets = account.tickets.where(reply_token: tags).includes(:requester).to_a
    reject!("reply addresses point at several tickets") if tickets.size > 1

    tickets.first
  end

  # Only the requester may reply by email. A reply joins the conversation and reopens a pending or solved ticket.
  def reply_from_requester(ticket)
    requester = ticket.requester
    from_requester = Helpdesk::InboundMail.from_addresses(mail).include?(requester.email)
    reject!("sender is not the requester of ticket #{ticket.id}") unless from_requester
    reject!("requester #{requester.id} is suspended") if requester.suspended?

    ticket.requester_update!(author: requester, comment: {body: text_body}, inbound_message_id: message_id)
  end

  # Mail to the plain support address opens a new ticket. A sender who is not yet a user becomes an unverified
  # customer. Email never verifies anyone.
  def open_ticket(account)
    sender = Helpdesk::InboundMail.sender_address(mail)
    reject!("no valid sender address") unless sender

    requester = nil
    created = false
    account.with_lock do
      requester, created = register_requester(account, sender)
      reject!("sender is #{requester.role}, not a customer") unless requester.customer?
      reject!("requester #{requester.id} is suspended") if requester.suspended?

      Ticket.open!(requester:, subject: Helpdesk::InboundMail.subject(mail), body: text_body, source: "email",
        inbound_message_id: message_id)
    end
    send_verification(requester) if created
  end

  # Sent only after the ticket is saved, so a mail server that refuses the message cannot lose the ticket.
  # If the email fails, the customer can ask for a new link with POST /email_verifications.
  def send_verification(requester)
    requester.send_email_verification!
  rescue StandardError => error
    logger.error("[helpdesk] verification email to customer #{requester.id} failed: #{error.class}: #{error.message}")
  end

  def register_requester(account, sender)
    User.customer_for_email!(account, name: Helpdesk::InboundMail.sender_name(mail, sender), email: sender)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => error
    reject!("sender could not be registered: #{error.record.errors.full_messages.to_sentence}")
  end

  def text_body
    @text_body ||= Helpdesk::InboundMail.text_body(mail)
  end

    def support_recipients(mail)

    def parse_address(text)
      Mail::Address.new(text.to_s)

    def sender_address(mail)
      address = from_addresses(mail).first

    def valid_address?(address)

    def sender_name(mail, address)

      name = address.split("@").first if name.blank?
      name.truncate(User::NAME_MAX_LENGTH, omission: "")
    end

    def subject(mail)
      clean_line(mail.subject).truncate(Ticket::SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH, omission: "").presence || "(no subject)"
    end

    # The plain-text message, stored as UTF-8 with line endings normalised.
    def text_body(mail)
      text = utf8(plain_text(mail)).delete("\u0000").gsub(/\r\n?/, "\n").strip

    end

    # Automated and list mail (auto-replies, bounces, notifications, newsletters). It is not a support request.
    def automated?(mail)
      names = mail.header.fields.map { |field| field.name.downcase }
      return true if names.any? { |name| name.start_with?("list-") } || names.intersect?(AUTOMATED_HEADERS)

      auto_submitted = mail.header["Auto-Submitted"]&.value.to_s.strip.downcase
      return true if auto_submitted.present? && auto_submitted != "no"
      return true if BULK_PRECEDENCE.include?(mail.header["Precedence"]&.value.to_s.strip.downcase)
      return true if mail.mime_type == "multipart/report"
      # An empty Return-Path (<>) is the null sender that bounces and auto-replies use.
      return true if mail.header["Return-Path"] && mail.header["Return-Path"].value.to_s.strip.empty?

      local = from_addresses(mail).first.to_s.split("@").first.to_s.split("+").first.to_s
      AUTOMATED_SENDER.match?(local)

    def plain_text(mail)
      parts = (mail.multipart? ? mail.all_parts.reject(&:multipart?) : [mail]).reject(&:attachment?)

      plain = parts.find { |part| part.mime_type.nil? || part.mime_type == "text/plain" }
      text = plain ? decode(plain) : ""
      return text if text.strip.present?

      html = parts.find { |part| part.mime_type == "text/html" }
      html ? html_to_text(decode(html)) : text
    end

    def decode(part)
      part.decoded.to_s
    rescue StandardError
      part.body.raw_source.to_s
    end

    # Turns line breaks and paragraph ends into newlines, drops script, style and head content, and
    # decodes entities.
    def html_to_text(html)
      html = html.gsub(%r{<br\s*/?>}i, "\n").gsub(%r{</(p|div|li|tr|h[1-6])\s*>}i, "\n")
      fragment = Loofah.fragment(html)
      fragment.xpath(".//script|.//style|.//head|.//title").each(&:remove)
      fragment.text(encode_special_chars: false)
    end

    def clean_line(text)
      utf8(text).delete("\u0000").gsub(/[[:space:]]+/, " ").strip

    def utf8(text)
      text = text.to_s
      case text.encoding
      when Encoding::UTF_8 then text.scrub("?")

# Turns mail sent to a business's support address into a ticket, and mail sent to a ticket's private reply
# address into a reply from the requester.
#
# A delivery is recorded as delivered only when it creates a comment. The comment stores the email's Message-ID,
# and only one comment can hold a given Message-ID. So a redelivery of a message that was delivered creates
# nothing, while a rejected, failed or interrupted delivery creates no comment and a later retry is processed.
#
# A rejected delivery's changes roll back and the inbound email is recorded as bounced.
class SupportMailbox < ApplicationMailbox
  DUPLICATE_INDEX = "index_comments_on_inbound_message_id".freeze

  # Raised to reject a delivery. Changes made inside a transaction roll back with it.
  class Rejected < StandardError; end

  def process
    deliver
  rescue Rejected => error
    reject_delivery(error.message)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique => error
    # A concurrent delivery of the same message saved its comment first. Its comment stands, so this one is a duplicate.
    raise unless error.message.include?(DUPLICATE_INDEX)

    reject_delivery("already delivered")
  end

  private

  def deliver
    reject!("already delivered") if Comment.exists?(inbound_message_id: message_id)
    reject!("automated or list mail") if Helpdesk::InboundMail.automated?(mail)

    account = business
    ticket = conversation(account)
    ticket ? reply_from_requester(ticket) : open_ticket(account)
  end

  def reject_delivery(reason)
    logger.info("[helpdesk] inbound email #{inbound_email.id} rejected: #{reason}")
    inbound_email.bounced!
  end

  def message_id
    inbound_email.message_id
  end

  # The one business this mail is for, found from every support-domain recipient (To, Cc and Bcc).
  # Mail addressed to several businesses is ignored, and so is mail addressed to none.
  def business
    subdomains = Helpdesk::InboundMail.support_recipients(mail).map(&:subdomain).uniq
    accounts = Account.where(subdomain: subdomains).to_a
    reject!("no business at the recipient addresses") if accounts.empty?
    reject!("addressed to #{accounts.size} businesses") if accounts.size > 1

    account = accounts.first
    reject!("business #{account.subdomain} is cancelled") if account.cancelled?
    account
  end

  # The ticket whose private reply address this mail was sent to, or nil. Mail to two different conversations
  # is ambiguous and is rejected.
  def conversation(account)
    tags = Helpdesk::InboundMail.support_recipients(mail).filter_map do |recipient|
      recipient.tag if recipient.subdomain == account.subdomain
    end
    tickets = account.tickets.where(reply_token: tags).includes(:requester).to_a
    reject!("reply addresses point at several tickets") if tickets.size > 1

    tickets.first
  end

  # Only the requester may reply by email. A reply joins the conversation and reopens a pending or solved ticket.
  def reply_from_requester(ticket)
    requester = ticket.requester
    from_requester = Helpdesk::InboundMail.from_addresses(mail).include?(requester.email)
    reject!("sender is not the requester of ticket #{ticket.id}") unless from_requester
    reject!("requester #{requester.id} is suspended") if requester.suspended?

    ticket.requester_update!(author: requester, comment: {body: text_body}, inbound_message_id: message_id)
  end

  # Mail to the plain support address opens a new ticket. A sender who is not yet a user becomes an unverified
  # customer. Email never verifies anyone.
  def open_ticket(account)
    sender = Helpdesk::InboundMail.sender_address(mail)
    reject!("no valid sender address") unless sender

    requester = nil
    created = false
    account.with_lock do
      requester, created = register_requester(account, sender)
      reject!("sender is #{requester.role}, not a customer") unless requester.customer?
      reject!("requester #{requester.id} is suspended") if requester.suspended?

      Ticket.open!(requester:, subject: Helpdesk::InboundMail.subject(mail), body: text_body, source: "email",
        inbound_message_id: message_id)
    end
    send_verification(requester) if created
  end

  # Sent only after the ticket is saved, so a mail server that refuses the message cannot lose the ticket.
  # If the email fails, the customer can ask for a new link with POST /email_verifications.
  def send_verification(requester)
    requester.send_email_verification!
  rescue StandardError => error
    logger.error("[helpdesk] verification email to customer #{requester.id} failed: #{error.class}: #{error.message}")
  end

  def register_requester(account, sender)
    User.customer_for_email!(account, name: Helpdesk::InboundMail.sender_name(mail, sender), email: sender)
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid => error
    reject!("sender could not be registered: #{error.record.errors.full_messages.to_sentence}")
  end

  def text_body
    @text_body ||= Helpdesk::InboundMail.text_body(mail)
  end

    LOCAL_PART = /\A(?<subdomain>[^+@\s]+)(?:\+(?<tag>[^+@\s]+))?\z/
    AUTOMATED_SENDER = /\A(mailer-daemon|postmaster|bounces?|(no|do-?not)-?reply)\z/
    # Set by autoresponders. X-Auto-Response-Suppress is left out: it asks auto-responders to stay quiet, and
    # some mail clients set it on ordinary messages.
    AUTOMATED_HEADERS = %w[x-autoreply x-autorespond].freeze
    BULK_PRECEDENCE = %w[bulk list junk auto_reply].freeze

    module_function

    # Every recipient on the support domain: To, Cc, Bcc and the forwarding headers the mail gem reads.
    # A malformed entry is skipped, so it cannot fail the whole delivery.
    def support_recipients(mail)
      domain = Helpdesk::Settings.support_domain
      mail.recipients.filter_map do |text|
        address = parse_address(text)
        next if address.nil? || address.domain.to_s.downcase != domain

        match = LOCAL_PART.match(address.local.to_s.downcase)
        Recipient.new(subdomain: match[:subdomain], tag: match[:tag]) if match
      end
    end

    # Lowercase addresses from the From header. Malformed entries are left out.
    def from_addresses(mail)
      Array(mail.from).filter_map { |text| parse_address(text)&.address&.downcase }
    end

    # The address in `text`, or nil when it cannot be parsed.
    def parse_address(text)
      Mail::Address.new(text.to_s)
    rescue StandardError
      nil
    end

    # The sender's address when it is a usable one, else nil.
    def sender_address(mail)
      address = from_addresses(mail).first
      address if valid_address?(address)
    end

    def valid_address?(address)
      address.present? && address.length <= 254 && URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP.match?(address)
    end

    # The From display name, or the address's local part when the sender gave no name.
    def sender_name(mail, address)
      name = clean_line(mail.from_address&.display_name)
      name = address.split("@").first if name.blank?
      name.truncate(User::NAME_MAX_LENGTH, omission: "")
    end

    def subject(mail)
      clean_line(mail.subject).truncate(Ticket::SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH, omission: "").presence || "(no subject)"
    end

    # The plain-text message, stored as UTF-8 with line endings normalised.
    def text_body(mail)
      text = utf8(plain_text(mail)).delete("\u0000").gsub(/\r\n?/, "\n").strip
      text.truncate(Comment::BODY_MAX_LENGTH, omission: "").presence || "(no message text)"
    end

    # Automated and list mail (auto-replies, bounces, notifications, newsletters). It is not a support request.
    def automated?(mail)
      names = mail.header.fields.map { |field| field.name.downcase }
      return true if names.any? { |name| name.start_with?("list-") } || names.intersect?(AUTOMATED_HEADERS)

      auto_submitted = mail.header["Auto-Submitted"]&.value.to_s.strip.downcase
      return true if auto_submitted.present? && auto_submitted != "no"
      return true if BULK_PRECEDENCE.include?(mail.header["Precedence"]&.value.to_s.strip.downcase)
      return true if mail.mime_type == "multipart/report"
      # An empty Return-Path (<>) is the null sender that bounces and auto-replies use.
      return true if mail.header["Return-Path"] && mail.header["Return-Path"].value.to_s.strip.empty?

      local = from_addresses(mail).first.to_s.split("@").first.to_s.split("+").first.to_s
      AUTOMATED_SENDER.match?(local)
    end

    # The text/plain part. If that part is blank, the text/html part converted to text.
    def plain_text(mail)
      parts = (mail.multipart? ? mail.all_parts.reject(&:multipart?) : [mail]).reject(&:attachment?)

      plain = parts.find { |part| part.mime_type.nil? || part.mime_type == "text/plain" }
      text = plain ? decode(plain) : ""
      return text if text.strip.present?

      html = parts.find { |part| part.mime_type == "text/html" }
      html ? html_to_text(decode(html)) : text
    end

    def decode(part)
      part.decoded.to_s
    rescue StandardError
      part.body.raw_source.to_s
    end

    # Turns line breaks and paragraph ends into newlines, drops script, style and head content, and
    # decodes entities.
    def html_to_text(html)
      html = html.gsub(%r{<br\s*/?>}i, "\n").gsub(%r{</(p|div|li|tr|h[1-6])\s*>}i, "\n")
      fragment = Loofah.fragment(html)
      fragment.xpath(".//script|.//style|.//head|.//title").each(&:remove)
      fragment.text(encode_special_chars: false)
    end

    def clean_line(text)
      utf8(text).delete("\u0000").gsub(/[[:space:]]+/, " ").strip
    end

    # Converts text to valid UTF-8, replacing bytes that cannot be read, so it can be stored.
    def utf8(text)
      text = text.to_s
      case text.encoding
      when Encoding::UTF_8 then text.scrub("?")
      when Encoding::BINARY then text.dup.force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8).scrub("?")
      else text.encode(Encoding::UTF_8, invalid: :replace, undef: :replace, replace: "?")
      end
    end
  end

class User < ApplicationRecord
  ROLES = %w[admin agent customer].freeze
  STAFF_ROLES = %w[admin agent].freeze
  NAME_MAX_LENGTH = 120
  MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 8
  EMAIL_VERIFICATION_TTL = 3.days
  PASSWORD_RESET_TTL = 2.hours

  has_secure_password
  belongs_to :account
  has_many :user_sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :requested_tickets, class_name: "Ticket", foreign_key: :requester_id, inverse_of: :requester,
    dependent: :destroy
  has_many :assigned_tickets, class_name: "Ticket", foreign_key: :assignee_id, inverse_of: :assignee,
    dependent: :nullify
  has_many :authored_comments, class_name: "Comment", foreign_key: :author_id, inverse_of: :author,
    dependent: :destroy
  has_many :group_memberships, inverse_of: :user, dependent: :destroy

  normalizes :email, with: ->(email) { email.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :name, presence: true, length: {maximum: NAME_MAX_LENGTH}
  validates :email, presence: true, length: {maximum: 254},
    format: {with: URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP}, uniqueness: {scope: :account_id}
  validates :role, inclusion: {in: ROLES}
  validates :password, length: {minimum: MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH}, allow_nil: true
  # Explicit password changes must include a password (a blank one would not change the digest).
  validates :password, presence: true, on: :new_password

  # Raised when suspending a user would leave the business without an active admin.
  class LastAdmin < StandardError; end

  scope :active, -> { where(suspended: false) }
  scope :staff, -> { where(role: STAFF_ROLES) }
  scope :admins, -> { where(role: "admin") }

  # Customers sign themselves up through a business's portal. The role is always "customer",
  # and the address is unverified until the emailed link is confirmed. An address with a pending
  # invitation belongs to that invitation, so it cannot be registered here.
  def self.register_customer!(account, name:, email:, password:)
    user = account.users.new(name:, email:, password:, role: "customer")
    account.with_lock do
      if account.invitations.pending.exists?(email: user.email)
        user.errors.add(:email, "is reserved for a pending invitation")
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, user
      end
      user.save!
    end
    user
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    # A concurrent registration with the same email won the unique index.
    user.errors.add(:email, "has already been taken")
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, user
  end

  # The customer behind an address that wrote in by email, registering one if the address is new. Returns
  # [user, created]. Email never verifies an address, so a new customer stays unverified until they confirm
  # the emailed link. Their password is random, so they set one with a password reset after verifying.
  # Existing users are returned as they are, whatever their role or status.
  def self.customer_for_email!(account, name:, email:)
    existing = account.users.find_by(email:)
    return [existing, false] if existing

    [register_customer!(account, name:, email:, password: Helpdesk::Token.generate), true]
  end

  # Token lookups match only unexpired tokens, and only within the given business.
  def self.with_email_verification_token(account, raw, now: Time.current)
    return if raw.blank?

    account.users.find_by(
      email_verification_token_digest: Helpdesk::Token.digest(raw),
      email_verification_sent_at: (now - EMAIL_VERIFICATION_TTL)..
    )
  end

  def self.with_password_reset_token(account, raw, now: Time.current)
    return if raw.blank?

    account.users.find_by(
      password_reset_token_digest: Helpdesk::Token.digest(raw),
      password_reset_sent_at: (now - PASSWORD_RESET_TTL)..
    )
  end

  # The group this person's tickets go to when they are assigned a ticket that has no group, or nil when they belong
  # to no group. Staff with memberships always have one default, so this is the group of their default membership.
  def default_group
    group_memberships.find_by(default: true)&.group
  end

  def owner?
    account.owner_id == id
  end

  def admin?
    role == "admin"
  end

  # Admins and agents work the business's tickets. Customers only see their own requests.
  def staff?
    STAFF_ROLES.include?(role)
  end

  def customer?
    role == "customer"
  end

  # Suspends or restores this user. Suspending signs the user out everywhere and clears their ticket
  # assignments. Neither changes a customer's request: the assignments are internal, and the tickets'
  # updated_at is left as it was. A business must keep one active admin, so the last one cannot be
  # suspended. The business row is locked so that two concurrent suspensions cannot both pass that check.
  def set_suspended!(value)
    transaction do
      account.lock!
      reload

      raise LastAdmin if value && admin? && account.users.admins.active.where.not(id:).none?

      update!(suspended: value)
      if value
        UserSession.where(user_id: id).delete_all
        Ticket.where(assignee_id: id).update_all(assignee_id: nil)
      end
    end
  end

  # Issues a new verification link, replacing any earlier one, and emails it.
  def send_email_verification!
    token = issue_email_verification_token!
    UserMailer.email_verification(self, token).deliver_now
  end

  def send_password_reset!
    token = issue_password_reset_token!
    UserMailer.password_reset(self, token).deliver_now
  end

  def verify_email!
    update!(verified: true, email_verification_token_digest: nil, email_verification_sent_at: nil)
  end

  # Sets a new password and signs out every session of this user. Used for both
  # password changes and password resets. Also invalidates any outstanding reset link.
  def set_password!(new_password)
    transaction do
      self.password = new_password.to_s
      self.password_reset_token_digest = nil
      self.password_reset_sent_at = nil
      save!(context: :new_password)
      UserSession.where(user_id: id).delete_all
    end
  end

  private

  def issue_email_verification_token!(now: Time.current)
    raw = Helpdesk::Token.generate
    update!(email_verification_token_digest: Helpdesk::Token.digest(raw), email_verification_sent_at: now)
    raw
  end

  def issue_password_reset_token!(now: Time.current)
    raw = Helpdesk::Token.generate
    update!(password_reset_token_digest: Helpdesk::Token.digest(raw), password_reset_sent_at: now)
    raw
  end
end

      user.save!
    end
    user

    # A concurrent registration with the same email won the unique index.

  def self.customer_for_email!(account, name:, email:)
    existing = account.users.find_by(email:)

  end

  def self.with_email_verification_token(account, raw, now: Time.current)
    return if raw.blank?

    account.users.find_by(
      email_verification_token_digest: Helpdesk::Token.digest(raw),
      email_verification_sent_at: (now - EMAIL_VERIFICATION_TTL)..
    )
  end

    return if raw.blank?

      password_reset_token_digest: Helpdesk::Token.digest(raw),
      password_reset_sent_at: (now - PASSWORD_RESET_TTL)..
    )
  end

  # to no group. Staff with memberships always have one default, so this is the group of their default membership.
  def default_group
    group_memberships.find_by(default: true)&.group
  end

  def owner?
    account.owner_id == id
  end

  def admin?
    role == "admin"
  end

  # Admins and agents work the business's tickets. Customers only see their own requests.
  def staff?
    STAFF_ROLES.include?(role)
  end

  def customer?
    role == "customer"
  end

  # Suspends or restores this user. Suspending signs the user out everywhere and clears their ticket
  # assignments. Neither changes a customer's request: the assignments are internal, and the tickets'
  # updated_at is left as it was. A business must keep one active admin, so the last one cannot be
  # suspended. The business row is locked so that two concurrent suspensions cannot both pass that check.
  def set_suspended!(value)
    transaction do
      account.lock!
      reload

      raise LastAdmin if value && admin? && account.users.admins.active.where.not(id:).none?

      update!(suspended: value)

  def send_email_verification!
    token = issue_email_verification_token!
    UserMailer.email_verification(self, token).deliver_now
  end

  def send_password_reset!
    token = issue_password_reset_token!
    UserMailer.password_reset(self, token).deliver_now
  end

  def verify_email!
    update!(verified: true, email_verification_token_digest: nil, email_verification_sent_at: nil)
  end

  # Sets a new password and signs out every session of this user. Used for both
  # password changes and password resets. Also invalidates any outstanding reset link.
  def set_password!(new_password)
    transaction do
      self.password = new_password.to_s
      self.password_reset_token_digest = nil
      self.password_reset_sent_at = nil
      save!(context: :new_password)
      UserSession.where(user_id: id).delete_all
    end
  end

  private

  def issue_email_verification_token!(now: Time.current)
    raw = Helpdesk::Token.generate
    update!(email_verification_token_digest: Helpdesk::Token.digest(raw), email_verification_sent_at: now)
    raw
  end

    raw = Helpdesk::Token.generate
    update!(password_reset_token_digest: Helpdesk::Token.digest(raw), password_reset_sent_at: now)
    raw
  end

# A staff member's place in a group. Someone can belong to several groups. Exactly one of their memberships is
# the default, which is the group a ticket gets when they are assigned it while it has no group.
#
# Changes that affect assignments are made while the business row is locked (see Account#lock!).
class GroupMembership < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :group, inverse_of: :group_memberships
  belongs_to :user, inverse_of: :group_memberships

  validates :user_id, uniqueness: {scope: :group_id, message: "already belongs to this group"}
  validate :in_same_business
  validate :user_must_be_staff

  # Assignments in this group to this person are no longer valid once the membership is gone.
  before_destroy :unassign_from_group
  # Someone who loses their default keeps their other memberships, so one of them becomes the default.
  after_destroy :promote_another_default, if: :default?

  # Adds a staff member to a group. The person's first membership is their default, whatever was asked for.
  # `default: true` makes this group the default and clears the old one. Returns the membership.
  # Unknown or invalid IDs raise RecordInvalid, with the error on the field that was wrong.
  def self.enroll!(account:, group_id:, user_id:, default: false)
    membership = nil
    account.with_lock do
      user = account.users.find_by(id: user_id) if client_id?(user_id)
      group = account.groups.find_by(id: group_id) if client_id?(group_id)
      membership = new(account:, group:, user:)
      membership.default = default || (user.present? && !user.group_memberships.exists?)
      membership.validate!
      membership.clear_other_defaults! if membership.default?
      membership.save!
    end
    membership
  end

  # Makes this group the person's default, replacing the old default.
  def make_default!
    transaction do
      account.lock!
      clear_other_defaults!
      update!(default: true)
    end
  end

  # Removes the person from the group. Assignments in the group are cleared, and the default moves if needed.
  def remove!
    transaction do
      account.lock!
      destroy!
    end
  end

  # Clears the default on this person's other memberships. Called before this membership becomes the default,
  # because the database allows only one default per person.
  def clear_other_defaults!
    GroupMembership.where(user_id:, default: true).where.not(id:).update_all(default: false)
  end

  private

  def in_same_business
    return if group.nil? || user.nil?

    errors.add(:user_id, "must belong to this business") if user.account_id != account_id
    errors.add(:group_id, "must be a group of this business") if group.account_id != account_id
  end

  def user_must_be_staff
    return if user.nil? || user.staff?

    errors.add(:user_id, "must be an admin or agent")
  end

  def unassign_from_group
    Ticket.where(group_id:, assignee_id: user_id).update_all(assignee_id: nil)
  end

  def promote_another_default
    successor = user.group_memberships.where.not(id:).order(:id).first
    successor&.update!(default: true)
  end
end

module HelpdeskTestHelpers
  HEADER = "X-Helpdesk-Account"
  PASSWORD = "my-first-password"
  NEW_PASSWORD = "my-new-password"

  # Performs a request against the JSON API. Pass `account:` for the business
  # header and `token:` for the bearer session token.
  def api(method, path, body: nil, account: nil, token: nil)
    headers = {"Accept" => "application/json"}
    headers[HEADER] = account if account
    headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer #{token}" if token

    if body
      send(method, path, params: body, headers: headers, as: :json)
    else
      send(method, path, headers: headers)
    end
  end

  def json
    response.parsed_body
  end

  def signup(subdomain: "acme", name: "Acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: PASSWORD, admin_name: "Jo")
    api(:post, "/api/v1/account/create", body: {
      account: {name:, subdomain:, admin: {name: admin_name, email:, password:}}
    })
  end

  # Signs up a business and confirms the owner's email. Returns the owner.
  def verified_owner(subdomain: "acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: PASSWORD)
    signup(subdomain:, email:, password:)
    assert_response :created
    token = link_token(last_mail)
    api(:post, "/api/v1/email_verifications/confirm", body: {email_verification: {token:}}, account: subdomain)
    assert_response :ok
    Account.find_by!(subdomain:).users.find_by!(email:)
  end

  def sign_in(email: "jo@acme.test", password: PASSWORD, account: "acme")
    api(:post, "/api/v1/sessions", body: {session: {email:, password:}}, account:)
    assert_response :created
    json.dig("session", "token")
  end

  CUSTOMER_PASSWORD = "my-customer-password"

  # Registers a customer through the portal and confirms the emailed link. Returns the customer.
  def verified_customer(account: "acme", name: "Avery", email: "avery@example.test", password: CUSTOMER_PASSWORD)
    register_customer(account:, name:, email:, password:)
    assert_response :created
    token = link_token(last_mail)
    api(:post, "/api/v1/email_verifications/confirm", body: {email_verification: {token:}}, account:)
    assert_response :ok
    Account.find_by!(subdomain: account).users.find_by!(email:)
  end

  def register_customer(account: "acme", name: "Avery", email: "avery@example.test", password: CUSTOMER_PASSWORD)
    api(:post, "/api/v1/registrations", body: {user: {name:, email:, password:}}, account:)
  end

  def customer_token(account: "acme", email: "avery@example.test", password: CUSTOMER_PASSWORD)
    sign_in(email:, password:, account:)
  end

  def open_request(token:, subject: "Cannot download my receipt", body: "The download button does nothing.", account: "acme")
    api(:post, "/api/v1/requests", body: {request: {subject:, comment: {body:}}}, account:, token:)
    assert_response :created
    json.dig("request", "id")

    mail.body.decoded[/token=([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)/, 1]
  end

  def header(name)
    response.headers.to_h.transform_keys(&:downcase)[name.downcase]
  end

  # Temporarily sets environment variables for the duration of the block.
  def with_env(vars)
    saved = vars.keys.to_h { |key| [key, ENV[key]] }
    vars.each { |key, value| value.nil? ? ENV.delete(key) : ENV[key] = value }
    yield
  ensure
    saved.each { |key, value| value.nil? ? ENV.delete(key) : ENV[key] = value }
  end

# Delivers mail the way the SMTP server does: a raw RFC 822 message posted to the relay ingress.
module InboundMailHelpers
  INBOUND_PASSWORD = "relay-test-password"
  RELAY_PATH = "/rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails"

  def relay(raw, password: INBOUND_PASSWORD)
    headers = {"CONTENT_TYPE" => "message/rfc822"}
    if password
      headers["HTTP_AUTHORIZATION"] = ActionController::HttpAuthentication::Basic.encode_credentials("actionmailbox", password)
    end
    post(RELAY_PATH, params: raw.to_s, headers: headers)
    response
  end

  # A plain-text message. Pass `headers:` to add or override headers.
  def raw_mail(from: "Avery <avery@example.test>", to: "acme@support.example.test", cc: nil,
    subject: "Cannot download my receipt", body: "The download button does nothing.",
    message_id: "<#{SecureRandom.hex(8)}@example.test>", headers: {})
    fields = {from:, to:, cc:, subject:, message_id:}.compact
    mail = Mail.new(fields)
    mail.body = body
    headers.each { |name, value| mail.header[name] = value }
    mail.to_s
  end

  def inbound_emails
    ActionMailbox::InboundEmail.order(:id)
  end

    Account.find_by!(subdomain:).tickets
  end

  def ticket_for(subject)
    account_tickets.find_by!(subject:)

module HelpdeskTestHelpers
  HEADER = "X-Helpdesk-Account"
  PASSWORD = "my-first-password"
  NEW_PASSWORD = "my-new-password"

  # Performs a request against the JSON API. Pass `account:` for the business
  # header and `token:` for the bearer session token.
  def api(method, path, body: nil, account: nil, token: nil)
    headers = {"Accept" => "application/json"}
    headers[HEADER] = account if account
    headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer #{token}" if token

    if body
      send(method, path, params: body, headers: headers, as: :json)
    else
      send(method, path, headers: headers)
    end
  end

  def json
    response.parsed_body
  end

  def signup(subdomain: "acme", name: "Acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: PASSWORD, admin_name: "Jo")

    })
  end

    assert_response :created
    token = link_token(last_mail)

    assert_response :ok

  end

  end

  def customer_token(account: "acme", email: "avery@example.test", password: CUSTOMER_PASSWORD)
    sign_in(email:, password:, account:)
  end

  # Opens a request as the customer behind `token`. Returns the request's ID.
  def open_request(token:, subject: "Cannot download my receipt", body: "The download button does nothing.", account: "acme")
    api(:post, "/api/v1/requests", body: {request: {subject:, comment: {body:}}}, account:, token:)

  # Temporarily sets environment variables for the duration of the block.
  def with_env(vars)
    saved = vars.keys.to_h { |key| [key, ENV[key]] }
    vars.each { |key, value| value.nil? ? ENV.delete(key) : ENV[key] = value }
    yield
  ensure
    saved.each { |key, value| value.nil? ? ENV.delete(key) : ENV[key] = value }
  end

# Delivers mail the way the SMTP server does: a raw RFC 822 message posted to the relay ingress.
module InboundMailHelpers
  INBOUND_PASSWORD = "relay-test-password"
  RELAY_PATH = "/rails/action_mailbox/relay/inbound_emails"

  def relay(raw, password: INBOUND_PASSWORD)
    headers = {"CONTENT_TYPE" => "message/rfc822"}
    if password
      headers["HTTP_AUTHORIZATION"] = ActionController::HttpAuthentication::Basic.encode_credentials("actionmailbox", password)
    end
    post(RELAY_PATH, params: raw.to_s, headers: headers)
    response
  end

  # A plain-text message. Pass `headers:` to add or override headers.
  def raw_mail(from: "Avery <avery@example.test>", to: "acme@support.example.test", cc: nil,
    subject: "Cannot download my receipt", body: "The download button does nothing.",
    message_id: "<#{SecureRandom.hex(8)}@example.test>", headers: {})
    fields = {from:, to:, cc:, subject:, message_id:}.compact
    mail = Mail.new(fields)
    mail.body = body
    headers.each { |name, value| mail.header[name] = value }
    mail.to_s
  end

  def inbound_emails
    ActionMailbox::InboundEmail.order(:id)
  end

    account_tickets.find_by!(subject:)
  end

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# An invitation for a person to join a business as an admin or agent. The emailed link carries a
# single-use token. Only its digest is stored, so a leaked database does not reveal usable links.
#
# Status is derived from the timestamps: accepted, then revoked, then expired (past expires_at),
# and otherwise pending. At most one pending invitation exists for an address in a business.
class Invitation < ApplicationRecord
  TTL = 7.days
  STATUSES = %w[pending accepted revoked expired].freeze
  # The same answer for an unknown, expired, used or revoked link, so links cannot be probed.
  INVALID_LINK_MESSAGE = "This invitation link is invalid or has expired.".freeze

  # Raised when an invitation is already accepted or revoked, so it can no longer be resent or revoked.
  class Closed < StandardError
    attr_reader :status

    def initialize(status)
      @status = status
      super("This invitation was already #{status}.")
    end
  end

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :invited_by, class_name: "User", optional: true
  belongs_to :accepted_user, class_name: "User", optional: true

  # The raw token exists only on the instance that issued it, for the email. It is never stored.
  attr_accessor :token

  normalizes :email, with: ->(email) { email.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :email, presence: true, length: {maximum: 254}, format: {with: URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP}
  validates :role, inclusion: {in: User::STAFF_ROLES, message: "must be admin or agent"}
  validate :email_available, on: %i[create reissue]

  scope :pending, ->(now = Time.current) {

      role: "customer", verified: true)
    @ticket = Ticket.open!(requester: @customer, subject: "Receipt", body: "Download does nothing")
  end

    assert_no_difference ["Ticket.count", "Comment.count"] do
      assert_raises(ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid) do
        Ticket.open!(requester: @customer, subject: "Receipt", body: " ")
      end
    end
  end

    @ticket.requester_update!(author: @customer, comment: {body: "Thanks, it works now"}, solve: true)

    assert_equal "pending", @ticket.reload.status

Unpermitted params are only logged, and bounced mail is asserted through `inbound_emails.pluck(:status)`. I have enough context to design this, so I'll write the tests first and watch them fail before implementing.

Design decisions, based on the existing code:
- **Closed status** is added to `Ticket::STATUSES`. That gives `?status=closed` on both `/tickets` and `/requests` for free, and it follows the `already_<status>` 422 pattern from invitations.
- **Merge** runs under the business row lock, the same lock the code already uses for assignments and group changes. Because of that lock, a concurrent reply can't land after the close.
- **Assignment cleanup** (suspension, membership removal, group deletion) already uses `update_all`, so it bypasses any closed-ticket guard. I'll leave it alone and test it.
- **Email to a closed ticket** is rejected as a bounce. It doesn't open a new ticket.
