require "test_helper"

class TicketMergesTest < ApiIntegrationTest
  setup do
    @saved_password = ENV["RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD"]
    ENV["RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD"] = INBOUND_PASSWORD
    @owner = verified_owner
    @owner_token = sign_in
    verified_customer
    @avery_token = customer_token
    @duplicate = open_request(token: @avery_token, subject: "Cannot download my receipt",
      body: "The download button does nothing.")
    @original = open_request(token: @avery_token, subject: "Receipt download fails",
      body: "Same problem as my other request.")
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear
  end

  teardown { ENV["RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD"] = @saved_password }

  def merge(source, body, token: @owner_token)
    api(:post, "/api/v1/tickets/#{source}/merge", body: {merge: body}, account: "acme", token:)
  end

  def staff_update(id, body, token: @owner_token)
    api(:patch, "/api/v1/tickets/#{id}", body: {ticket: body}, account: "acme", token:)
  end

  def add_staff(name, email, role: "agent")
    Account.find_by!(subdomain: "acme").users.create!(name:, email:, password: PASSWORD, role:, verified: true)
  end

  def ticket(id)
    Ticket.find(id)
  end

  def assert_error(status, code)
    assert_response status
    assert_equal code, json.dig("error", "code")
  end

  # An email ticket from Avery, opened through the relay. Returns the ticket.
  def open_email_ticket(subject)
    relay(raw_mail(subject:))
    assert_response :no_content
    ticket_for(subject)
  end

  # --- Merging ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  test "a merge returns the closed duplicate as source and the surviving ticket as target" do
    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original})

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal @duplicate, json.dig("source", "id")
    assert_equal "closed", json.dig("source", "status")
    assert_equal @original, json.dig("source", "merged_into_id")
    assert_equal @original, json.dig("target", "id")
    assert_equal "open", json.dig("target", "status")
    assert_nil json.dig("target", "merged_into_id")
  end

  test "a ticket that was never merged shows a null merged_into_id to staff and to the customer" do
    api(:get, "/api/v1/tickets/#{@original}", account: "acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert json["ticket"].key?("merged_into_id")
    assert_nil json.dig("ticket", "merged_into_id")

    api(:get, "/api/v1/requests/#{@original}", account: "acme", token: @avery_token)
    assert json["request"].key?("merged_into_id")
    assert_nil json.dig("request", "merged_into_id")
  end

  test "a solved duplicate can be merged too" do
    staff_update(@duplicate, {status: "solved"})

    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original})

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "closed", ticket(@duplicate).status
  end

  test "any staff member can merge, including an agent" do
    pat = add_staff("Pat", "pat@acme.test")
    pat_token = sign_in(email: "pat@acme.test")

    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original}, token: pat_token)

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "closed", ticket(@duplicate).status
  end

  test "the target may be sent as a string of digits" do
    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original.to_s})

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal @original, ticket(@duplicate).merged_into_id
  end

  test "the closed ticket keeps its own comments, and they are not moved to the target" do
    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original})

    assert_equal ["The download button does nothing.", "Merged into ticket #{@original}."],
      ticket(@duplicate).comments.pluck(:body)
    assert_equal ["Same problem as my other request.", "Ticket #{@duplicate} was merged into this ticket."],
      ticket(@original).comments.pluck(:body)
  end

  test "each side gets a private note by default, written by the staff member" do
    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original})

    source_note = ticket(@duplicate).comments.last
    target_note = ticket(@original).comments.last
    assert_equal false, source_note.public
    assert_equal false, target_note.public
    assert_equal @owner.id, source_note.author_id
    assert_equal @owner.id, target_note.author_id
  end

  test "default notes are hidden from the customer on both tickets" do
    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original})

    api(:get, "/api/v1/requests/#{@duplicate}/comments", account: "acme", token: @avery_token)
    assert_equal ["The download button does nothing."], json["comments"].pluck("body")
    api(:get, "/api/v1/requests/#{@original}/comments", account: "acme", token: @avery_token)
    assert_equal ["Same problem as my other request."], json["comments"].pluck("body")
  end

  test "staff can write each note and make either one public" do
    merge(@duplicate, {
      target_id: @original,
      source_comment: {body: "Continuing in ticket #{@original}.", public: true},
      target_comment: {body: "Duplicate checked.", public: false}
    })

    assert_response :ok
    api(:get, "/api/v1/requests/#{@duplicate}/comments", account: "acme", token: @avery_token)
    assert_equal ["The download button does nothing.", "Continuing in ticket #{@original}."], json["comments"].pluck("body")
    assert_equal [true, false], ticket(@original).comments.pluck(:public).last(2)
    assert_equal "Duplicate checked.", ticket(@original).comments.last.body
    api(:get, "/api/v1/requests/#{@original}/comments", account: "acme", token: @avery_token)
    assert_equal ["Same problem as my other request."], json["comments"].pluck("body")
  end

  test "a public note on the surviving ticket is shown to the customer" do
    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original, target_comment: {body: "Merged, see this ticket.", public: true}})

    api(:get, "/api/v1/requests/#{@original}/comments", account: "acme", token: @avery_token)
    assert_equal ["Same problem as my other request.", "Merged, see this ticket."], json["comments"].pluck("body")
  end

  test "a blank note text falls back to the default text" do
    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original, source_comment: {body: "  ", public: true}})

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "Merged into ticket #{@original}.", ticket(@duplicate).comments.last.body
  end

  test "merge notes send no email, even public ones on an email ticket" do
    email_ticket = open_email_ticket("Email duplicate")
    ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.clear

    merge(email_ticket.id, {target_id: @original,
      source_comment: {body: "Continuing elsewhere.", public: true},
      target_comment: {body: "Public too.", public: true}})

    assert_response :ok
    assert_empty ActionMailer::Base.deliveries
  end

  test "the surviving ticket keeps its status, assignee and reply address" do
    staff_update(@original, {status: "pending", assignee_id: @owner.id})
    before = ticket(@original).attributes.slice("status", "assignee_id", "reply_token", "source", "requester_id")
    reply_address = ticket(@original).reply_address

    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original})

    assert_response :ok
    after = ticket(@original).attributes.slice("status", "assignee_id", "reply_token", "source", "requester_id")
    assert_equal before, after
    assert_equal reply_address, ticket(@original).reply_address
  end

  test "a failed note rolls the whole merge back" do
    too_long = "x" * (Comment::BODY_MAX_LENGTH + 1)

    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original, target_comment: {body: too_long}})

    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert_equal "open", ticket(@duplicate).status
    assert_nil ticket(@duplicate).merged_into_id
    assert_equal 1, ticket(@duplicate).comments.count
    assert_equal 1, ticket(@original).comments.count
  end

  test "staff cannot close a ticket directly, only by merging it" do
    staff_update(@duplicate, {status: "closed"})

    assert_response :unprocessable_entity
    assert json.dig("error", "details", "status").present?
    assert_equal "open", ticket(@duplicate).status
  end

  # --- Refused merges -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

  test "customers cannot merge tickets" do
    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original}, token: @avery_token)

    assert_error :forbidden, "forbidden"
    assert_equal "open", ticket(@duplicate).status
  end

  test "a ticket can only be merged into another ticket of the same customer" do
    verified_customer(email: "sam@example.test", name: "Sam")
    sam_ticket = open_request(token: customer_token(email: "sam@example.test"), subject: "Login loop")

    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: sam_ticket})

    assert_error :unprocessable_entity, "validation_failed"
    assert json.dig("error", "details", "target_id").present?
    assert_equal "open", ticket(@duplicate).status
    assert_equal 1, ticket(@duplicate).comments.count
    assert_equal 1, ticket(sam_ticket).comments.count
  end

  test "a ticket cannot be merged into itself" do
    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @duplicate})

    assert_error :unprocessable_entity, "validation_failed"
    assert_equal "open", ticket(@duplicate).status
  end

  test "an unknown target is refused" do
    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: 999_999})

    assert_error :unprocessable_entity, "validation_failed"
    assert json.dig("error", "details", "target_id").present?
  end

  test "a target that is not a ticket ID is refused" do
    [nil, "abc", 1.5, true, [@original], {id: @original}, "0", "-3"].each do |bad|
      merge(@duplicate, {target_id: bad})
      assert_error :unprocessable_entity, "validation_failed"
      assert json.dig("error", "details", "target_id").present?, "expected target_id to be refused: #{bad.inspect}"
    end
    assert_equal "open", ticket(@duplicate).status
  end

  test "a request without a merge object is refused" do
    api(:post, "/api/v1/tickets/#{@duplicate}/merge", body: {target_id: @original}, account: "acme", token: @owner_token)

    assert_error :bad_request, "parameter_missing"
  end

  test "malformed notes are refused and nothing is merged" do
    [
      {target_id: @original, source_comment: "Continuing elsewhere."},
      {target_id: @original, source_comment: {body: {text: "hi"}}},
      {target_id: @original, target_comment: {body: "Fine", public: "maybe"}}
    ].each do |body|
      merge(@duplicate, body)
      assert_error :unprocessable_entity, "validation_failed"
    end
    assert_equal "open", ticket(@duplicate).status
    assert_equal 1, ticket(@duplicate).comments.count
  end

  test "a closed ticket cannot be merged again, and keeps its first link" do
    third = open_request(token: @avery_token, subject: "Login loop", body: "Login keeps looping.")
    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original})

    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: third})

    assert_error :unprocessable_entity, "already_closed"
    assert_equal @original, ticket(@duplicate).merged_into_id
    assert_equal 2, ticket(@duplicate).comments.count
    assert_equal 1, ticket(third).comments.count
  end

  test "a closed ticket cannot be the target of a merge" do
    third = open_request(token: @avery_token, subject: "Login loop", body: "Login keeps looping.")
    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original})

    merge(third, {target_id: @duplicate})

    assert_error :unprocessable_entity, "validation_failed"
    assert json.dig("error", "details", "target_id").present?
    assert_equal "open", ticket(third).status
  end

  # --- Surviving tickets and later merges ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  test "merging the surviving ticket later keeps the original links" do
    third = open_request(token: @avery_token, subject: "Receipt problem again", body: "Still failing.")
    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original})

    merge(@original, {target_id: third})

    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal @original, ticket(@duplicate).merged_into_id
    assert_equal third, ticket(@original).merged_into_id
    assert_equal "closed", ticket(@original).status
    assert_nil ticket(third).merged_into_id
    assert_equal "open", ticket(third).status
  end

  test "the customer can follow a chain of merges from each closed request" do
    third = open_request(token: @avery_token, subject: "Receipt problem again", body: "Still failing.")
    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original})
    merge(@original, {target_id: third})

    api(:get, "/api/v1/requests/#{@duplicate}", account: "acme", token: @avery_token)
    assert_equal @original, json.dig("request", "merged_into_id")
    api(:get, "/api/v1/requests/#{@original}", account: "acme", token: @avery_token)
    assert_equal third, json.dig("request", "merged_into_id")
  end

  test "replies by email still reach the surviving ticket" do
    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original})

    relay(raw_mail(to: ticket(@original).reply_address, body: "It still fails on Safari"))

    assert_response :no_content
    assert_equal "It still fails on Safari", ticket(@original).comments.reload.last.body
  end

  # --- Closed tickets: listings, edits and email ----------------------------------------------------------------

  test "both the staff and the customer views filter for closed tickets" do
    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original})

    api(:get, "/api/v1/tickets?status=closed", account: "acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_equal [@duplicate], json["tickets"].pluck("id")
    api(:get, "/api/v1/requests?status=closed", account: "acme", token: @avery_token)
    assert_equal [@duplicate], json["requests"].pluck("id")
    api(:get, "/api/v1/requests?status=open", account: "acme", token: @avery_token)
    assert_equal [@original], json["requests"].pluck("id")
  end

  test "the closed ticket is still listed and readable by staff" do
    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original})

    api(:get, "/api/v1/tickets", account: "acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_includes json["tickets"].pluck("id"), @duplicate
    api(:get, "/api/v1/tickets/#{@duplicate}", account: "acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_response :ok
    assert_equal "closed", json.dig("ticket", "status")
    api(:get, "/api/v1/tickets/#{@duplicate}/comments", account: "acme", token: @owner_token)
    assert_equal 2, json["count"]
  end

  test "a closed ticket refuses staff edits of every kind" do
    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original})

    [
      {comment: {body: "Hello?"}},
      {comment: {body: "Private hello", public: false}},
      {status: "open"},
      {status: "pending"},
      {priority: "high"},
      {assignee_id: @owner.id},
      {group_id: nil}
    ].each do |body|
      staff_update(@duplicate, body)
      assert_error :unprocessable_entity, "already_closed"
    end
    assert_equal "closed", ticket(@duplicate).status
    assert_equal 2, ticket(@duplicate).comments.count
    assert_nil ticket(@duplicate).assignee_id
    assert_equal "normal", ticket(@duplicate).priority
  end

  test "a closed request refuses the customer's reply and solve" do
    merge(@duplicate, {target_id: @original})

    api(:patch, "/api/v1/requests/#{@duplicate}", body: {request: {comment: {body: "Any update?"}}},
      account: "acme", token: @avery_token)

    api(:patch, "/api/v1/requests/#{@duplicate}", body: {request: {status: "solved"}},
      account: "acme", token: @avery_token)
    assert_error :unprocessable_entity, "already_closed"

    assert_equal 2, ticket(@duplicate).comments.count
  end

  test "a closed email ticket rejects replies to its reply address, and no ticket is opened" do
    email_ticket = open_email_ticket("Email duplicate")
    merge(email_ticket.id, {target_id: @original})

  test "suspending the assignee clears the assignment on a closed ticket" do

class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  # "closed" is set only by merging the ticket into another (see merge_into!). A closed ticket is readable, but it
  # takes no edits and no email replies.
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved closed].freeze
  PRIORITIES = %w[normal high].freeze
  # "portal" for requests opened in the portal. "email" for tickets opened from inbound mail, whose public
  # replies are emailed to the requester.
  SOURCES = %w[portal email].freeze
  SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH = 255

  # Passed as `group_id:`, `assignee_id:` or `priority:` to staff_update! to leave that field as it is.
  UNCHANGED = Object.new.freeze

  # Raised when an edit is attempted on a closed ticket. Nothing is saved.
  class Closed < StandardError
    def initialize(ticket)
      super(if ticket.merged_into_id
        "This ticket is closed. It was merged into ticket #{ticket.merged_into_id}."
      else
        "This ticket is closed."
      end)
    end
  end

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User", inverse_of: :requested_tickets
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true, inverse_of: :assigned_tickets
  belongs_to :group, optional: true
  # The ticket this one was merged into. Set only on closed tickets. It is kept if that ticket is merged later.
  belongs_to :merged_into, class_name: "Ticket", optional: true
  has_many :comments, -> { order(:created_at, :id) }, inverse_of: :ticket, dependent: :destroy

  validates :subject, presence: true, length: {maximum: SUBJECT_MAX_LENGTH}
  validates :status, inclusion: {in: STATUSES}
  validates :priority, inclusion: {in: PRIORITIES}
  validates :source, inclusion: {in: SOURCES}

  before_validation :assign_reply_token, on: :create

  # Most recently active first. Public replies and status changes touch updated_at.
  scope :recent_first, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }

  # Case-insensitive search through subjects and public comments. Private notes are not searched.
  # The text is literal: % and _ match themselves, not wildcards. The EXISTS subquery means a
  # ticket appears once however many comments match.
  def self.search(text)
    pattern = "%#{sanitize_sql_like(text)}%"
    where(<<~SQL.squish, pattern:)
      tickets.subject ILIKE :pattern OR EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM comments
        WHERE comments.ticket_id = tickets.id AND comments.public = TRUE AND comments.body ILIKE :pattern
      )
    SQL
  end

  # Opens a request for `requester` with its first comment. Both are saved, or neither is. `inbound_message_id`
  # is the Message-ID of the email the request came from, if any.
  def self.open!(requester:, subject:, body:, source: "portal", inbound_message_id: nil)
    ticket = new(account: requester.account, requester:, subject:, status: "open", source:)
    ticket.comments.build(author: requester, body:, public: true, inbound_message_id:)
    ticket.save!
    ticket
  end

  def email?
    source == "email"
  end

  def closed?
    status == "closed"
  end

  # The private address for this conversation, e.g. acme+<token>@support.example.test. Mail sent here is a reply
  # from the requester, and it lands on this ticket.
  def reply_address
    Helpdesk::Settings.support_address(account.subdomain, tag: reply_token)
  end

  # A customer's update: an optional public reply, optionally marking the request solved.
  # A reply reopens a pending or solved request, unless the same update marks it solved.
  # `inbound_message_id` is the Message-ID of the email the reply came in, if any.
  # A closed request takes no reply and raises Closed.
  def requester_update!(author:, comment: nil, solve: false, inbound_message_id: nil)
    transaction do
      lock_for_update!
      comments.create!(author:, body: comment[:body], public: true, inbound_message_id:) if comment.present?
      update!(status: solve ? "solved" : "open") if comment.present? || solve
    end
  end

  # A staff update: an optional reply (public unless marked private), optional status change, and optional
  # routing and priority. Routing is the group (an ID, or nil to ungroup the ticket), and the assignee (an active
  # staff member's ID, or nil to unassign). A reply alone never changes the status. Routing and priority are
  # internal, so they do not touch updated_at. A public reply on an email ticket is also emailed to the requester,
  # after the update is saved. A closed ticket raises Closed, and "closed" cannot be set here: merge to close.
  def staff_update!(author:, comment: nil, changes: {}, group_id: UNCHANGED, assignee_id: UNCHANGED,
    priority: UNCHANGED)
    reply = nil
    transaction do
      lock_for_update!
      refuse_manual_close!(changes)
      reply = comments.create!(author:, body: comment[:body], public: comment.fetch(:public, true)) if comment.present?
      update!(changes) if changes.any?
      route_internally!(group_id:, assignee_id:) unless group_id.equal?(UNCHANGED) && assignee_id.equal?(UNCHANGED)
      prioritize_internally!(priority) unless priority.equal?(UNCHANGED)
    end
    email_reply_to_requester(reply) if reply&.public?
  end

  # Merges this duplicate into `target_id`, another ticket of the same customer, and closes it. This ticket's
  # comments and reply address stay as they are, and so do the target's status, assignee and reply address. The
  # target is not changed beyond its updated_at. Each side gets a note: `source_note` goes on this ticket and
  # `target_note` on the target. A note is private unless `public: true`. A blank body gets the default text.
  # Merge notes send no email. The merge is saved whole or not at all. Returns [source, target].
  def merge_into!(target_id:, author:, source_note: {}, target_note: {})
    target = nil
    transaction do
      lock_for_update!
      target = find_merge_target!(target_id)
      comments.create!(author:, **note_attributes(source_note, "Merged into ticket #{target.id}."))
      target.comments.create!(author:, **note_attributes(target_note, "Ticket #{id} was merged into this ticket."))
      update!(status: "closed", merged_into: target)
    end
    [self, target.reload]
  end

  private

  def assign_reply_token
    self.reply_token ||= SecureRandom.hex(16)
  end

  # Suspended requesters are cut off from the email channel, so their replies are not sent.
  def email_reply_to_requester(reply)
    return unless email? && !requester.suspended?

    TicketMailer.reply(reply).deliver_later
  end

  # Every edit starts here. The business row is locked first, the same lock that assignment and group changes take,
  # and then the ticket is reloaded. So the closed check sees the state the edit will change, and a merge cannot land
  # between the check and the save. Raises Closed for a closed ticket.
  def lock_for_update!
    account.lock!
    reload
    raise Closed, self if closed?
  end

  # A ticket is closed only by merging it, so a staff update cannot set that status.
  def refuse_manual_close!(changes)
    return unless changes.stringify_keys["status"] == "closed"

    fail_validation!(:status, "can only be closed by merging the ticket into another")
  end

  # The ticket to merge into. It must be another ticket of this business, from the same customer, and not closed.
  def find_merge_target!(target_id)
    target = account.tickets.find_by(id: target_id)
    fail_validation!(:target_id, "must be a ticket of this business") if target.nil?
    fail_validation!(:target_id, "must be a different ticket") if target.id == id
    fail_validation!(:target_id, "must belong to the same customer") if target.requester_id != requester_id
    fail_validation!(:target_id, "must be a ticket that is not closed") if target.closed?
    target
  end

  # The attributes of one merge note. It is private unless public is true, and a blank body gets the default text.
  def note_attributes(note, default_body)
    {body: note[:body].presence || default_body, public: note.fetch(:public, false)}
  end

  # Sets the group and the assignee together, so that every assignee belongs to the ticket's group:
  #   - An assignee must belong to the ticket's group. Assigning anyone else is refused.
  #   - Assigning someone to a ticket with no group gives the ticket that person's default group, if they have one.
  #     Someone with no groups can still be assigned, and the ticket stays ungrouped.
  #   - Moving the ticket to another group clears an assignee who does not belong to it.
  #   - Clearing the assignee leaves the group. Clearing the group also clears the assignee, so the two cannot be
  #     set together in one update.
  # The changes are made with update_columns, so updated_at is untouched.
  def route_internally!(group_id:, assignee_id:)
    # Locking the business serialises this with group and membership changes, so the memberships checked
    # below still hold when the ticket is saved. The ticket is reloaded under that lock.
    account.lock!
    reload

    group_given = !group_id.equal?(UNCHANGED)
    assignee_given = !assignee_id.equal?(UNCHANGED)
    new_group = group_given ? find_group(group_id) : group
    new_assignee = assignee_given ? find_assignee(assignee_id) : assignee

    if group_given && new_group.nil?
      if assignee_given && new_assignee
        fail_validation!(:assignee_id, "cannot be set in the same update that clears the group")
      end
      new_assignee = nil
    elsif group_given
      if assignee_given
        ensure_member!(new_assignee, new_group) if new_assignee
      else
        new_assignee = nil if new_assignee && !member?(new_assignee, new_group)
      end
    elsif new_group
      ensure_member!(new_assignee, new_group) if assignee_given && new_assignee
    elsif assignee_given && new_assignee
      new_group = new_assignee.default_group
    end

    update_columns(group_id: new_group&.id, assignee_id: new_assignee&.id)
    association(:group).reset
    association(:assignee).reset
  end

  # The group with this ID in the business, or nil for nil. An unknown ID is refused.
  def find_group(group_id)
    return if group_id.nil?

    found = account.groups.find_by(id: group_id) if self.class.client_id?(group_id)
    found || fail_validation!(:group_id, "must be a group of this business")
  end

  # The active staff member with this ID in the business, or nil for nil. Customers, suspended staff and
  # unknown IDs are refused.
  def find_assignee(assignee_id)
    return if assignee_id.nil?

    found = account.users.staff.active.find_by(id: assignee_id) if self.class.client_id?(assignee_id)
    found || fail_validation!(:assignee_id, "must be an active staff member of this business")
  end

  def member?(user, group)
    GroupMembership.exists?(group:, user:)
  end

  def ensure_member!(user, group)
    return if member?(user, group)

    fail_validation!(:assignee_id, "must belong to the ticket's group")
  end

  def fail_validation!(field, message)
    errors.add(field, message)
    raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, self
  end

  # Sets the priority with update_columns, which skips updated_at, as assignment does. update_columns
  # skips validations, so the value is checked here.
  def prioritize_internally!(value)
    unless PRIORITIES.include?(value)
      errors.add(:priority, "must be normal or high")
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, self
    end

    update_columns(priority: value)
  end

end

               "target_comment":{"body":"Duplicate checked.","public":false}}}

The response is `200 {source, target}`, both as staff see them. The rules are:

- **The duplicate is closed.** Its status becomes `closed` and its `merged_into_id` becomes `57`. It stays readable: its
  comments and reply address are unchanged, and both staff and the customer can list it with `?status=closed`.
- **The surviving ticket is not changed** beyond its `updated_at`. Its status, assignee, and reply address stay as they
  were, and no comments move to it.
- **Notes.** Each side gets one note. `source_comment` goes on the duplicate and `target_comment` on the surviving ticket.
  Both are private unless `"public": true`. A blank or missing `body` gets default text ("Merged into ticket 57." and
  "Ticket 42 was merged into this ticket."). Notes are written by the staff member who merged, and merging sends no email,
  even for a public note on an email ticket.
- **Closed tickets take no edits.** Any staff update or customer reply to a closed ticket returns `422 already_closed`,
  and nothing is saved. This covers replies, status, group, assignee and priority changes. Its own comments can still be read.
- **Closed tickets take no email.** Mail to a closed ticket's reply address is bounced. It does not open a new ticket. Mail
  to the surviving ticket's reply address works as before.
- **Assignment cleanup still applies.** Suspending a user, removing them from a group, or deleting a group clears their
  assignments on closed tickets too.
- **Refused merges** return `422 validation_failed` with `details.target_id`, and nothing is saved. The target must be
  another ticket of this business, from the same customer, and not closed. A duplicate that is already closed returns
  `422 already_closed`.
- **Later merges keep the original links.** If the surviving ticket is merged into a third ticket, it closes and points
  at that ticket. The duplicate still points at the ticket it was first merged into.
- **Atomic.** The merge and both notes are saved together, or not at all. A note that fails validation (for example, a body
  over 10,000 characters) rejects the whole merge.

messages.content:
Everything is in place and verified. Here is the summary before I submit.

## Summary

Staff can now merge a duplicate into another ticket of the same customer with `POST /api/v1/tickets/:id/merge`. The full suite passes: 375 runs, 0 failures. That includes 37 new tests in `test/integration/ticket_merges_test.rb`.

### What changed
- **Migration** `20261119070000`: adds `closed` to the status check constraint, and a `merged_into_id` self-reference. Its foreign key nullifies on delete, and two check constraints enforce that a pointer is set only on a closed ticket and never points at itself. Rollback and re-apply both work.
- **`Ticket`**:
  - `merge_into!` closes the duplicate and writes both notes in one transaction.
  - Every edit (staff update, customer reply) takes the business lock, reloads, and raises `Ticket::Closed` if the ticket is closed.
  - Staff cannot set `closed` directly. Only a merge closes a ticket.
- **Comment**: a validation refuses new comments on a closed ticket, as a backstop.
- **Mailbox**: a reply to a closed ticket's reply address is bounced. It opens no new ticket.
- **Serializers and routes**: `merged_into_id` appears in both staff and customer views. Both views accept `?status=closed`.
- **README**: the merge rules, the new error code, and the updated status lists.

### Verification
- Mutation checks: removing the edit guard, the mailbox rescue, or the cleanup exemption each makes the right tests fail.
- Live Puma with curl: the spec's example body returns `{source, target}`. Edits to the closed ticket return `422 already_closed`. Both views filter for closed. Unmerged records show `null`.
- Concurrency: 12 parallel merges of the same duplicate gave one 200 and eleven `already_closed`, with no 500s.
- Deletion: deleting a customer or purging the business removes merged pairs without a constraint error.

### Decisions you may want to review
- **Edits to a closed ticket** return `422 already_closed`, following the existing `already_accepted` / `already_cancelled` pattern.
- **Refused merges** (unknown target, another customer, self, closed target) return `422 validation_failed` on `target_id`, not 404. This matches how other body IDs are handled here.
- **Assignment cleanup** is read as: suspension, group-membership removal, and group deletion still clear assignments on closed tickets. The merge itself leaves the duplicate's assignee as it was.
- **Blank note text** falls back to default text rather than being refused.
- **Concurrency**: all ticket edits now take the business row lock, as assignment and group changes already did. This serializes edits per business. I chose it over per-ticket locks to keep lock ordering consistent and avoid deadlocks.
- **Activity**: the duplicate's `updated_at` changes when it closes, because a status change counts as customer-visible activity. So it moves to the top of the customer's list.
- **Rollback** of the migration converts closed tickets to `solved`, which loses the merge link.

I did not commit anything. The repository's history doesn't track these files, so the changes are left in the working tree.
